name: streamed-lifetime-aware-worksets

initialFailedRun.cause: test harness ReferenceError: `after` was scoped inside try and referenced in finally
initialFailedRun.architecturalInterpretation: No architecture claim was made from this run. Five of six new streamed tests had already passed; the failure was repaired as a test-scope bug and retained in lineage.

measuredExternalPeakDeltaBytes.interpretation: The broader Node external metric moved in the opposite direction and is not used as evidence for a whole-process memory win.

measuredRssPeakDeltaBytes.interpretation: RSS is recorded as a secondary noisy process/allocator observation, not promoted as the primary claim.

normalTimingMs.interpretation: No speedup is supported. Streamed execution was approximately tied and slightly slower on the hosted median.

singleBodyCounterexample.interpretation: Streaming cannot reduce peak runtime-body bytes when the request needs only one indivisible body.

mechanism.wholeClosure: Materialize all missing closure runtime bodies before executing the deterministic topological order.
mechanism.streamed: Materialize the next ready missing runtime body, execute it immediately, then retain it under policy or release/null the runtime reference before proceeding. Dependency outputs remain available after dependency runtime bodies are released.
mechanism.retainedBudget: The byte ceiling remains a hard retained-cache budget. One currently executing miss may temporarily exist in addition to retained cache.

strongestSupportedClaim: In this deterministic typed-array workspace harness, streamed lifetime-aware workset execution reduced the median live ArrayBuffer peak for the seven-body report from 962,268 B to 837,720 B while materializing the same total 962,268 B and producing the same deterministic result hash. The single-body counterexample showed zero peak savings. Normal hosted timing did not improve.
truthBoundary: This does not prove universal physical RAM reduction.
This does not prove total RSS reduction or external-memory reduction.
This does not prove universal speedup; the streamed report median was slightly slower in the measured timing run.
Result/output object memory is outside the declared runtime-body byte accounting.
Forced-GC memory probes are separated from normal timing probes.
The current peak floor is bounded by the largest indivisible required capability body, which is the 837,720 B search index in this fixture.
This does not prove created RAM, free compute, or free energy.
nextGate: Test segmented/chunked oversized capability bodies so a single atomic body no longer defines the minimum possible active runtime-body peak.
